methodology: Ranks compare current-season regular-season production, not scouting grades or predicted future strength. Higher weighted standardized production scores rank better; missing metrics are unranked and ties share a rank.

QB combines passing and rushing EPA/play, net yards/play and turnover rate. RB combines EPA/opportunity, scrimmage yards/game and touchdowns/game. WR/TE combine EPA/target, receiving yards/game and touchdowns/game.
OL is a protection/run-game proxy: sack rate and RB rushing EPA/carry. Quarterback, backs and scheme also affect it; it is not an isolated blocking grade.
DL includes DE, DT, NT, DL, EDGE and OLB labels, ranked on sacks, tackles for loss and QB hits/game. Off-ball LB uses tackles for loss, passes defended, solo tackles and forced fumbles/game.

CB and safety rankings measure passes defended, interceptions and forced fumbles/game. They do not measure coverage quality or penalize unthrown targets. Players labeled only DB are excluded from CB/S because the subtype is unknown.

All players who recorded stats contribute to their actual team at the time. These are season unit results, not an injury-adjusted ranking of today’s starters. Per-game metrics use the team’s recorded games, not sums of individual appearances.
